note: A schedule of RECURRING RELEASE PATTERNS, not a list of confirmed dates.
It exists so the blackout logic, the tiering and the surprise maths can be
exercised end to end on a machine with no network and no data subscription.
Each series carries a `certainty`, and that field is the honest part:
confirmed          the exact date and time came from a feed. Nothing in
this bundled file is ever `confirmed` -- only ingestion
from a live source can set it.
scheduled_pattern  the DAY is structural and published as a rule by the
statistical agency (payrolls on the first Friday, ISM
on the first business day). The time is the agency's
standing release time. These drive blackout windows.
approximate        the day is a typical-case guess inside a window. These
do NOT drive blackouts -- a stale guess that blocks
trading on the wrong day is worse than no calendar,
and one that clears the real day is worse still. They
surface as 'confirm this date' advisories instead.
Central bank meeting dates are published a year or more ahead by each bank.
They are NOT reproduced here as literal dates, because a bundled date that
is wrong reads exactly like one that is right. The cadence patterns below
generate advisory placeholders; the documented ingestion hook is how real
dates get in.

series.name: Non-Farm Payrolls
series.note: BLS releases the Employment Situation on the third Friday after the reference week, which is the first Friday of the month in all but a handful of years.

series.name: FOMC rate decision
series.note: Eight meetings a year on a six-to-seven week cadence, decision at 14:00 New York. The cadence is real; the individual dates are not confirmed here.

series.name: ECB monetary policy decision
series.note: Decision at 14:15 Frankfurt, press conference 14:45. Frankfurt is CET/CEST, and its summer-time window is NOT the same as New York's.

series.name: Bank of Japan policy decision
series.note: Tokyo has observed no summer time since 1951, so JST is UTC+9 all year. The release time drifts relative to a London-based blackout only because London itself moves.

series.name: Canada Labour Force Survey
series.note: Ottawa is in the same DST regime as New York, so one offset serves both.

series.name: RBA cash rate decision
series.note: Stored in UTC rather than Australia/Sydney: southern-hemisphere summer time runs the opposite way round and is not implemented in core.tzrules. Pretending otherwise would be the exact failure this file exists to avoid.
